reports.notes: All 10 found; but its P0 sy-tabix premise is wrong

false_claims.claim: P0-2 / lesson 3: 'sy-tabix is not set by the language in a LOOP AT itab without an INTO/WA target', therefore this loop may silently fail to raise the dialog height (worst defect in the file).
false_claims.why_wrong: sy-tabix IS set in a target-less LOOP AT itab (L3, L6 count correctly). The proposed failure mode is invented; the real, minor issue is only the target-less idiom being fragile style, not a P0 correctness bug.

false_claims.claim: 'PERFORM target not existing passes the syntax check but dumps at runtime (PERFORM target absence is a runtime, not compile-time, error).
false_claims.why_wrong: A PERFORM naming a non-existent FORM is caught by the ABAP syntax check (SE38/ATC) as an error, not deferred to runtime; the certainty is unjustified.

reports.notes: Strong: 9/10; treats one-shot assembly as correct design

false_claims.claim: Screen logic 'must hang the modules D_0100_PBO and D_0100_PAI' (repeated in 3.2-1 and in the naming-contract discussion).
false_claims.why_wrong: The source declares MODULE pbo / MODULE pai, so the screen 100 flow can only call PBO/PAI. D_0100_PBO is a stale generated comment header (L6), not the module name; the report turns a comment artifact into a required binding.

false_claims.claim: Header table lists CALL SCREEN as part of this file's GUI form.
false_claims.why_wrong: The source contains no CALL SCREEN; it lives in zsalv_csqt_create_container.abap (L15). The report's own code block for that FM is otherwise verbatim-correct.

false_claims.claim: gr_container is 'a TOP-INCLUDE global TYPE REF TO cl_gui_simple_container'.
false_claims.why_wrong: No TOP include exists in the corpus; the type is asserted as fact but is unverifiable and not derivable from either available file.

defects.anchor: L34-L36, L80, L148 (no PROCESS statement in file)

false_claims.claim: Fix for the dead okcode: '(a) add lv_okcode = sy-ucomm. at the module start; (b) drop the buffer and use sy-ucomm everywhere' (also 3.3-1 'why' and P0-1 fix).
false_claims.why_wrong: Both fixes cannot work: sy-ucomm is CHAR1 (internal SAP GUI convention), so assigning it to lv_okcode TYPE syst_ucomm and comparing against 'OPEN'/'CLOSE'/'STOP' truncates to one char and never matches. The correct type is sy-okcode (CHAR10) / CASE sy-okcode. The report therefore misses the length defect entirely - the same CHAR1 error report 2 caught in the sibling file.

false_claims.claim: 'PBO/PAI okcode only exists in sy-ucomm' and keeping an lv_okcode buffer is 'a common idiom for deferring okcode handling inside PAI'.
false_claims.why_wrong: There is no such idiom; the PAI command field is sy-okcode. sy-ucomm is a CHAR1 flag, not a function-code holder, so the premise of the whole 3.3-1 'why' section is wrong.

false_claims.claim: 'The program really depends on three external objects: screen 0100, PF-STATUS 0100, TITLEBAR 0100' (also item 23).
false_claims.why_wrong: SET SCREEN 100 activates screen 100, not 0100; only the PF-STATUS and TITLEBAR are named 0100. The report itself quotes SET SCREEN 100 elsewhere.

false_claims.claim: 3.2-4 why: 'putting the gate last is deliberate - only after all four steps succeed is it set, so a failed step can retry on the next PBO'.
false_claims.why_wrong: show_message does not exit the module, so lv_init is set even after a failed step and there is no retry path; the report contradicts its own P0-3.

false_claims.claim: Item 18: 'liveness is checked in three places in three different forms (NOT ... IS INITIAL / IS INITIAL / NOT ... IS INITIAL)'.
false_claims.why_wrong: Only two forms exist in the file (L88 and L119); the third listed item is a plain null check, so the count is inflated.
